title: Adopt Path Matches Bootstrap Settle on macOS
description: Fix the adopt path of the shared-worktree fleet so a macOS machine that adopts a tar-extracted tree ends up like one that went through bootstrap-settle: (1) join --adopt and its --dry-run rename non-NFC names to NFC before planning, reusing the bootstrap-settle code; (2) a differing executable bit of an otherwise identical file follows the normal conflict rule instead of being adopted silently; (3) --plan of the provision script no longer extracts the bootstrap archive into an empty worktree (or the next real run settles a tree the script itself extracted). Tests first, next to the replica tests; update the module README. Evidence: tickets 26/11/09/SHARED-WORKTREE-FLEET-OVER-NFS (g1-m07-join.md).
summary: join --adopt renames non-NFC names to NFC before planning through the shared normaliseNamesV1 (bootstrap), its dry run reads them as NFC and lists them; equal bytes with a differing executable bit are no longer adopted as identical but follow the stale/edit/conflict rule; the provision scripts no longer extract on --plan with an empty worktree and mark a tree they extracted (.cache/f/bootstrap-extract) so a later run settles it instead of adopting. Tests added first (vectors, Python oracle, adoption, CLI, provision shell); 410 tests pass over the replica, adopt, bootstrap, relocate and topology files through repo tools exec bun. Not done: the graph route repo run could not get a capacity grant, the PowerShell script was not executed (no pwsh). Details in summary.md.
